People ask how to start one and I tell them the truth, which is that the first three are bad and you throw them away. Not literally: you keep them, and once a decade you open one and wince. But you throw away the idea that they were the thing. The thing starts when you stop performing for the reader you imagine looking over your shoulder, and that takes about three notebooks of practice, and nobody I know has skipped it. The hand gets tired before the performance does, which is the mercy of the medium.

There is a version of this advice that turns into a product, and I want to be careful not to give it. Nobody needs a particular pen. The paper does not matter. What matters is that the tool cannot be edited, so the sentence you wrote is the sentence you wrote, and you have to live with it long enough to see what it actually says. Every editing tool I have used lets me hide from that. The notebook does not, and that is the whole of its virtue, and it is enough.
